info.name: Premisave Developer Service
info.description:
Premisave Developer Service: developer accounts, businesses, apps, API keys and the public /v1 entry.

Setup: import the collection, set base_url_dev, run Sign up (or Sign in); the token is saved as access_token. Confirm the email address (folder Email and password) before applying for a business. Run Apply for a business (folder 01), fill in and submit its application, then Create app (sandbox): the key and secret are saved as api_key and api_secret and used by folder 05. One account can apply for many businesses; business_id is the one the calls work on. Folder 06 needs admin_api_key (DEVELOPER_INTERNAL_API_KEY on the server) and developer_id.

To hand a production app to another developer account, or to take up an approved business by its merchant number, use folder 03: a code is emailed to the business owner, who shares it with you, and you confirm it with the otp variable.

A secret is shown once. If you lose it, create or rotate a key.

request.description: Required: email, firstName, lastName, password (at least 10 characters), country (2 letters) and acceptTerms (must be true). Optional: middleName, phoneNumber (7 to 15 digits), companyName, marketingOptIn. A username is generated for you. 409 EMAIL_TAKEN if the email is used. The account is created PENDING and the answer carries only message, next (CONFIRM_EMAIL), status (PENDING) and confirmationEmailSent: no token and no account data. A confirmation email is sent when a mail server is set, and confirming it makes the account ACTIVE. Show data.message and tell the developer to open the confirmation link. Sign in answers 403 ACCOUNT_PENDING until the email is confirmed, so open the link from the email (or the log when log-links is on) first, then run Sign in.
5 failed attempts lock the account for 15 minutes (423 ACCOUNT_LOCKED). 403 ACCOUNT_PENDING when the password is right but the email is not confirmed yet (data.next is CONFIRM_EMAIL).

The body is the image file itself, not form data: in Postman choose Body, binary, and pick a JPEG, PNG or WebP file of at most 5 MB (set the Content-Type header to match). The picture is stored in Cloudinary and data.profilePictureUrl is the address to show. A new picture replaces the old one. 400 VALIDATION_FAILED if the file is not an image, 413 PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE if too big, 503 UPSTREAM_UNAVAILABLE if Cloudinary is not set up or cannot be reached.
Removes the picture from Cloudinary and the account. Safe to repeat.

item.name: 00 Email and password

request.description: Paste the token from the link in the confirmation email (...verify-email?token=THIS). Works once. 400 INVALID_TOKEN if unknown, used or expired. With DEVELOPER_MAIL_LOG_LINKS=true and no mail server the link is in the service log.
409 INVALID_STATE if already confirmed. 429 RATE_LIMITED with retryAfterSeconds if asked within 60 seconds, or more than 5 times an hour.
No sign in needed. Always answers 200 with the same message, whether or not the address has an account.
Always answers 200 with the same message. If the address has an active account a link to {portal}/reset-password?token=... is emailed. Good for 60 minutes.
Uses the token from the reset email. A weak password is refused before the link is spent. Every session ends; sign in again with the new password and set developer_password to it.

item.description: Links arrive by email and point at the portal. Copy the token from the link into email_token.

item.name: 00 Social sign in

request.description: The providers switched on in this service and their public client IDs: { providers: [...], clientIds: { google, facebook, github } }. No secrets are returned.

Body: the Google ID token (the credential from Google Identity Services). Get one by running oauth-test/social-login-test.html in Get the token only mode, or from the OAuth 2.0 Playground with the openid and email scopes. The service checks it with Google and requires that it was issued to GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID. Returns the usual session plus newAccount and provider. A first sign in with a new email creates the account. 403 ACCOUNT_PENDING (data.next is CONFIRM_EMAIL) when the account still has to confirm its email, 401 OAUTH_FAILED when the provider rejects the token, 409 ACCOUNT_EXISTS when the provider does not vouch for an email that already has an account, 422 OAUTH_EMAIL_REQUIRED when the provider gives no usable email.

Body: a Facebook user access token. Get one from the test page (Facebook button, or paste one) or from the Graph API Explorer with the email permission, using the same app as FACEBOOK_CLIENT_ID. The service asks Facebook whether the token was issued to this app. Facebook never vouches for the email, so a new account starts PENDING until the email is confirmed. Returns the usual session plus newAccount and provider. A first sign in with a new email creates the account. 403 ACCOUNT_PENDING (data.next is CONFIRM_EMAIL) when the account still has to confirm its email, 401 OAUTH_FAILED when the provider rejects the token, 409 ACCOUNT_EXISTS when the provider does not vouch for an email that already has an account, 422 OAUTH_EMAIL_REQUIRED when the provider gives no usable email.

Body: token is the one-time code GitHub puts in the address when it sends you back (the test page shows it in Get the token only mode). GitHub does not give a browser an access token, so the service trades the code with the client secret. A code works once and for about 10 minutes. Returns the usual session plus newAccount and provider. A first sign in with a new email creates the account. 403 ACCOUNT_PENDING (data.next is CONFIRM_EMAIL) when the account still has to confirm its email, 401 OAUTH_FAILED when the provider rejects the token, 409 ACCOUNT_EXISTS when the provider does not vouch for an email that already has an account, 422 OAUTH_EMAIL_REQUIRED when the provider gives no usable email.

item.description: The provider token is made in the browser, so no OAuth screen is needed here. Run oauth-test/social-login-test.html (Get the token only mode), copy the token into the matching collection variable and send the request. Google sends an ID token, Facebook an access token, GitHub a one-time code.

item.name: 01 Businesses and onboarding
item.description: One account can apply for many businesses. Each has its own merchant number and its own application. business_id is the business the calls in this folder work on.

request.description: Adds a business to the account and opens its application as a draft. Only name and country are required; the contact email defaults to the account email. An account can apply for many businesses (up to DEVELOPER_MAX_BUSINESSES, 10 by default). Applying again for the same name and country answers 409 BUSINESS_EXISTS with the existing businessId. 403 EMAIL_NOT_VERIFIED until the email address is confirmed. The reply has a nextStep that says what to do next.

The same account applying for a second business. It gets its own business id, merchant number and application. The id is saved as other_business_id, so the calls below keep working on the first business.
Every business of the account with its status, application summary and nextStep.
One business. 404 BUSINESS_NOT_FOUND if it is not on this account.
Status, form, documents, returnItems, missing items and readyToSubmit for this business.

request.description: Saves the form. Send only what changed. walletAccountNumber is the Premisave wallet account (the owner's email) that this business is linked to: the owner can follow the application, and later see the merchant number, from that wallet, and the code for moving an app or sharing the business is emailed there. It is required to submit. If you are applying for someone else's business, set onBehalf to true, say your role in applicantRole (for example Developer at the agency) and upload an authorisation letter. The tax pin and director ID numbers are stored masked in the replies.

Form data, not JSON. In Postman choose Body, form-data, then pick the file on the file row. type can be written as business registration, business-registration or BUSINESS_REGISTRATION. 400 if the file is empty, over 5 MB or not a PDF, PNG or JPEG. Needs Google Drive configured on the wallet, otherwise 503.

item.name: 03 Transfers and sharing

request.description: Starts moving a production app to another developer account, named by the email it signs in with. A six digit code is emailed to the address linked to the business (the wallet account named on its application, or the business contact email). You never see the code: the business owner has to share it with you. The code lasts 15 minutes and 5 wrong tries close the request. Only production apps can be moved. When it is confirmed the app keeps its merchant number and wallet link, its API keys are revoked, the other account is given use of the business, and you keep the business and its other apps.

Send the six digit code the business owner shared with you. Works once. 400 OTP_INVALID for a wrong code (attemptsLeft says how many tries remain), 410 OTP_EXPIRED after the time is up, 409 INVALID_STATE when the request is already done or closed.

Emails a fresh code for a request that is still open. The old code stops working and the tries start again. At most one code a minute, and ten requests an hour (429 RATE_LIMITED, retryAfterSeconds says when).
Closes a request that has not been confirmed. Nothing moves.
Your latest requests (direction OUTGOING) and the apps on their way to you (direction INCOMING). An incoming one shows the sender's address in part only and nothing about the code.
One request. status is PENDING, COMPLETED, CANCELLED or EXPIRED.

item.name: Claim a business by merchant number

request.description: Asks to use a business that another account applied for and that is approved and live, so you can go live with the same merchant number. Nothing moves: the business owner shares the emailed code and you confirm it with Confirm transfer, then create a production app for the business (businessId). A number that does not exist and a business that is not live get the same answer, 404 BUSINESS_NOT_FOUND, and wrong numbers count towards a limit of ten requests an hour.

item.description: Move a production app to another developer account, or take up an approved business by its merchant number. Both are confirmed with a code emailed to the address linked to the business.

request.description: The secret is shown once. Up to 5 active keys per app.
The old key keeps working for 24 hours as ROTATING. Run it from the key you want to replace.

item.description: The same endpoints under /api/v1/admin, with the bearer token of an account whose role is ADMIN. Sign in as that account first. Every path in folder 06 works here by replacing /internal/admin with /api/v1/admin and dropping the X-API-Key header.
